title: Framing Effect
equation: Frame Gap = Response Rate A - Response Rate B
hook: Same facts, different words, totally different decision. How you say it matters more than you think.
statement: The exact same fact leads people to different decisions depending on how you frame it.
explainer: Doctors pick a treatment more often when told it has 90% survival than when told 10% mortality. Same number. Your customers do this too, so honest framing is a real advantage.
sop: Pick the key fact you need customers to understand.
Write it two ways, as a gain and as a loss.
Never frame something in a way that misleads.
equation_example: Frame A, loss-framed, converts at 18%. Frame B, gain-framed, at 11%. Frame Gap = 18 - 11 = 7 percentage points. A bigger gap means wording is doing heavy lifting, so standardize the winner. Near 0 means focus on clarity over wording.
question: Take one line from your sales page and rewrite it with the opposite frame.
closing_statement: The same facts can lead to opposite decisions.
caption:
Principle Nº 296: Framing Effect

Same facts, different words, totally different decision. How you say it matters more than you think.

The exact same fact leads people to different decisions depending on how you frame it.

Your turn: Take one line from your sales page and rewrite it with the opposite frame.
